english.notes:
(i) Section 32(3) of the Human Tissue Act 2004 provides that a person who engages in an activity to which section 31(1) or (2) applies does not commit the offence if he is designated by the Human Tissue Authority as a person who may lawfully engage in the activity.
(ii) Section 32(6) and (7) of the Act provides when payment in money or money's worth shall be treated as not being a reward.
(iii) Section 32(8) of the Act provides that controlled material is any material which
(a) consists of or includes human cells,
(b) is, or is intended to be removed, from a human body, and (c) is intended to be used for the purpose of transplantation.
(iv) Section 32(8)(d) and (9) of the Act provides that gametes, embryos, and material which is the subject of property because of an application of human skill are not controlled material.
(v) Section 32(10) of the Act deals with bodies of deceased persons.
(vi) Section 32(11) of that Act provides that reward means any description of financial or other material advantage.
(vii) Extended jurisdiction - see section 32A of the Human Tissue Act 2004 regarding the committing of this offence outside the UK by a UK national or a person habitually resident in England and Wales.

other.penalty:
Either way

Summary: maximum 6 / 12 months imprisonment and / or fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 3 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Notes
(i) The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 32(4)(a)(i) of the Human Tissue Act 2004 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.
(ii) On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
